messages:
maya: Heads-up — runtime-8 p95 jumped from ~400ms to ~1.2s around 14:02 UTC. KV prefix hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~22% within ~3m. Anyone else seeing this?

alex: Yep, dashboards show throughput down ~25%. Traces point to batching backlog and a bunch of kernels falling back to slower paths. @prashant can you pull kernel-selection logs?

prashant: On it. Quick note — we rolled out a tenant flag earlier: tenant-42 enabled quantize-agg at 13:58 (rollout service). Could be correlated.

deploy-bot: rollout/flags/tenant-42 quantize-agg -> true (started 13:58 UTC, 10% -> 100% by 14:00)

maya: I pulled runtime logs from the affected pods. Lots of kernel selection fallbacks when quantized model artifacts are requested. Example snippet: 
```
KERNEL_SELECT: time=14:01:02 model=star-13b size=4096 selected=avx2_generic reason=quantize-path-missing shard=rt-8
KERNEL_SELECT: time=14:01:03 model=star-13b size=2048 selected=avx2_generic reason=quantize-path-missing shard=rt-8
```

alex: Batcher logs show small batch sizes because responses are slower: `batcher.queue_depth` hovered 1..3 instead of usual 8..16. That increases per-request latency.

prashant: KV metrics from the shard: 
```
kv.hits=12345
kv.misses=45678
evictions=9876
prefix_p99_memory=2048KB
```
Eviction rate spiked at 14:01.

ingrid: Any sign of a noisy neighbor? Which tenant had the big cardinality? @lina

lina: tenant-42 ran a load test yesterday and then turned on dense prompts + quantize-agg. Current metric: `prefix.cardinality=1.2M` (orders of magnitude above typical ~50k).

maya: Hypothesis: enabling quantize-agg changed memory layout / kernel path which increased per-prefix footprint on the KV store. That caused cache pressure -> rapid evictions -> prefix hit-rate collapse -> batching fragility -> latency spike.

alex: Immediate mitigation options: rollback the quantize flag for tenant-42, temporarily throttle tenant-42 traffic, or increase KV shard budget. Rollback seems fastest.

prashant: I can rollback flag now and also re-pin kernel selection to preferred kernels for runtime-8. Kernel pin config is at `/etc/runtime/kernel-pins.yaml`. Which do we do first?

ingrid: Rollback the flag first, then monitor 5m. If hit-rate recovers, follow with kernel pin/patch and a controlled re-roll with updated heuristics.

maya: prashant — please proceed. Also capture heap/kv profiles during the tail of the incident for postmortem.

prashant: Rolling back quantize-agg for tenant-42 now.

prashant: rollback/flags/tenant-42 quantize-agg -> false at 14:06 UTC (by prashant)

maya: Thanks. Watching metrics. :eyes:

deploy-bot: flag/tenant-42 quantize-agg set -> false by prashant at 14:06 UTC

alex: 14:09 update: p95 back down to ~420ms, kv.hitrate ~88%, evictions trending down. Looks like rollback helped.

lina: Filed a guardrail issue: infra#5234 — do not auto-enable quantize-agg when `prefix.cardinality > 500k`. Also suggests a gradual canary for memory footprint.

maya: Action items: 1) Add kernel-selection telemetry alert when >5% of requests fall back to non-optimized kernels. 2) Add prefix-cardinality guardrail before enabling heavy memory features. 3) Capture and store heap+kv profiles for the affected runtime.

prashant: I'll open a PR for kernel pins + a canary test harness. I'll attach the profiles once uploaded.

ingrid: Great work triaging. We'll write a short incident note and move to a full postmortem if anything reoccurs. Thanks all.

maya: quick note for postmortem — consider tuning batching heuristics to avoid queue collapse when backend latency rises (adaptive max-batch based on observed kernel latencies).

alex: Agreed. Also add an alert for sudden eviction_rate > 1000/min on a single shard.

lina: adding those to infra backlog. I'll sync with product on tenant flag rollout UX.

prashant: uploading heap and kv snapshots to s3://redwood-incidents/1851234567/ now.

ingrid: moving this thread to incidents once we have the postmortem doc. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
